description.en-US: A price rule for a product template or one of its variants (BR §6.12). Deferred fields: §6.12 also lists price_list_id, currency_id, sales_channel_id, customer_id and customer_group_id; none of those five entities exists yet, so declaring the columns would create foreign keys to nothing and imply multi-currency, price-list and per-customer pricing that is not built. Add each alongside the entity it points at. Note there is deliberately no composite_uniques, unlike every sibling entity: several price rows per product is the point of this table, since a scheduled change is two rows with different effective ranges.

The template this price applies to, when the price is the base rule for a whole product line. Exactly one of product_template_id and product_variant_id is set: neither leaves the rule unreachable, both make precedence ambiguous. See BR §6.12 rule 1.
The variant this price applies to. A variant rule overrides the template rule for that variant. See BR §6.12 rule 2.
The amount. Currency is not modelled yet: inventory_currency does not exist, so every price is in the tenant's single currency. See the deferred fields note below.
First day this price applies. Null means it applies from the beginning of time, which is the normal case for a product's standing price.
Last day this price applies. Null means it does not expire. A scheduled price change is two rows, not an edit, so that the outgoing price stays auditable.
Pricing workflow state. Only an approved row is ever applied to a product; draft lets a price be prepared without taking effect. See BR §6.12.
